To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

foliar application of 24-EPBL and 28-hoBL at the concentration of 2.0 μM alleviated the adverse effect of excess Zn2+ on radish plant growth and improved photosynthetic attributes and antioxidant system in radish plants.
the foliar application of BRs alleviated the adverse effects of Zn2+ toxicity in radish by enhancing the antioxidant defense and improving the photosynthetic efficiency.
EBL and HBL, two brassinosteroid compounds, were able to alleviate the adverse effects of excess Zn2+ on radish plants by improving the growth, photosynthetic pigmentation, and antioxidant status.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the alleviation of Zn2+ toxicity in radish plants by application of EBL and HBL.
the ameliorative effect of BRs against the adverse effects of excess Zn2+ on growth and physiological attributes of radish plants.
the first study that reports the amelioration of adverse effects of Zn2+ toxicity by BRs application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BRs application could be used as an efficient strategy to ameliorate Zn2+ toxicity in radish plants.
foliar application of EBL and HBL can be used to alleviate Zn2+ stress in radish plants.
BRs are effective in ameliorating Zn2+ stress in radish plants and EBL was found more effective than HBL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
foliar application of 24-EBL at 2 μM concentration could be a good strategy to mitigate the adverse effects of Zn2+ on radish plants.
foliar application of BRs could be used as a potential strategy to alleviate Zn2+ toxicity in radish plants.
foliar application of 24-EBL at 1 μM concentration is most effective in improving growth and physiological traits of radish plants exposed under Zn2+ toxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BRs can alleviate adverse effects of Zn2+ toxicity in radish plants and can be used as a tool to mitigate heavy metal stress in plants.
foliar application of EBL at 1.0 μm concentration is an efficient strategy to improve radish growth and alleviate Zn2+ toxicity in radish plants.
foliar application of BRs could be used as a tool to mitigate Zn2+ stress in radish and perhaps in other crops.
